turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi, how are things with you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you explain what an unreliable narrator is? We keep saying it in class and I just nod.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sure. It's when the person telling the story can't be fully trusted, because they lie, forget things, or misunderstand what's happening.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So the author does it on purpose?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, it's deliberate. The fun is that you slowly realize the story you've been told isn't quite what really happened.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is that like when a kid narrates and doesn't get

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Exactly, that's a classic example. The kid isn't lying, they just don't understand, and the reader sees more than they do.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, that's actually cool. I thought it was just a fancy word for a bad narrator.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Far from it. Done well, it's one of the cleverest tricks a writer can pull.
